title: In Clothes Called Fat
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Noko Hanazawa, an overweight office worker who eats to cope with stress, is tormented by a cruel coworker, Mayumi, who begins an affair with Noko's long-time boyfriend Saito to hurt her further. Convinced that being thin will make her happy, Noko starts dieting and slides into bulimia. This single-volume adult drama follows her decline without offering an easy resolution.
life_message: Self-worth tied to body size and others' approval leads to self-destruction; the story leaves the reader to find the alternative.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Worth judged by appearance and social standing at work, not inherent dignity.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Adults left to their own choices; no one intervenes effectively.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Workplace and romance dominate; family barely present.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Office pecking order and looks-based ranking among women.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Urban, secular modern Tokyo office life.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Job security and appearance conformity weigh against self-acceptance.

folkways.japan: Pressure on office ladies to conform in looks and behavior reflects 1990s Japanese corporate norms that the josei genre often examines.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer says the story avoids stating its themes and leaves interpretation to the reader.
delivery.note: The critique of beauty pressure emerges from Noko's decline rather than from any stated argument.

winners_losers: No one ends happy; Noko loses health and self, Mayumi and Saito gain little. Sympathy goes to Noko as a victim and agent of her decline.
